cards.title: Audit the colours of tokens.css and define the tokens of the dark theme
cards.body: Scope: read web/styles/tokens.css and the 5 screens of the Acme Notes web app (note list, editor, search, settings, sharing dialog). Steps: 1) inventory every colour in use (background, text, links, borders, note cards, tags, buttons, banners); 2) propose a dark palette as a table light token to dark token with hexadecimal values and the measured contrast of each text and background pair; 3) judge the real rendering on screenshots, never the code. Out of scope: changing the code or the mock-up yourself, writing copy. Acceptance criteria: every finding is located, measured and comes with a precise recommendation, and the verdict is unambiguous. Proof: a report with the annotated screenshots.

cards.title: Implement the CSS variables and the dark theme in tokens.css
cards.body: Scope: web/styles/tokens.css only, plus the CSS fixes strictly needed in the 5 screens. Steps: 1) turn the colours into custom properties on the root element and add the dark theme under [data-theme=dark]; 2) follow prefers-color-scheme when no explicit choice was made and set color-scheme for the native controls; 3) check the result at 380 px and 1440 px, with the keyboard and with a pointer; 4) leave no error or warning in the console of the browser. Out of scope: the API, the content, a redesign of the screens that are not named. Acceptance criteria: no regression of the existing screens, keyboard use works end to end and the console stays empty. Proof: the diff, the output of the tests and before and after screenshots.

cards.title: Add the light/dark toggle with a remembered choice, without a framework
cards.body: Scope: a toggle button in the shared header of the app and a small inline script in plain JavaScript. Steps: 1) read localStorage and prefers-color-scheme in an inline script of the head and set data-theme before the first paint, so that nothing flashes; 2) make the button reachable with the keyboard, with an accessible name and its pressed state; 3) leave no error or warning in the console of the browser. Out of scope: the server code, the copy of the interface, any new dependency. Acceptance criteria: the build passes, the rendering matches the reference on every screen named and nothing shifts while the page loads. Proof: the output of the build and screenshots of each state at both widths.

cards.title: Review of the dark mode code (CSS, script, accessibility)
cards.body: Scope: the diff of the cards c2 and c3, nothing else. Steps: 1) check that no hard-coded colour is left outside the variables and that the palette of the design card is the one applied; 2) reload each screen with a cold cache and confirm that the theme is set before the first paint; 3) number each finding and say how to reproduce it; 4) end with a verdict: validated, changes requested or blocked. Out of scope: fixing what you find yourself. Acceptance criteria: every criterion of the card reviewed is checked one by one and the verdict follows from the findings. Proof: the numbered findings and the commands that were run.

cards.title: Browser tests of dark mode on the 5 screens, on mobile and desktop
cards.body: Scope: the 5 screens of the web app in a real browser, at 380 px and 1440 px, in both themes. Steps: 1) walk through writing a note, searching, changing a setting and sharing a notebook in each theme; 2) switch the theme in the middle of each journey and check that the choice survives a reload; 3) keep the tests that were written in the suite of the project; 4) use the real application in a real browser, as a user would. Out of scope: fixing the bugs, judging the visual design. Acceptance criteria: every journey has a result, every bug can be reproduced from its steps and the new tests run in the suite. Proof: the test report, the output of the suite and a screenshot per bug.

cards.title: Visual critique of the dark rendering and of the contrast on real screenshots
cards.body: Scope: the screenshots of the 5 screens in the dark theme, compared with the light theme. Steps: 1) judge hierarchy, legibility of the note text, tags, focus rings and images; 2) measure the contrast of every pair that looks weak and report the figure; 3) judge the real rendering on screenshots, never the code. Out of scope: any fix, any change of the content. Acceptance criteria: no finding rests on taste alone, each one points at a screenshot that shows it. Proof: the list of findings with the screenshot that proves each of them.

cards.title: Document dark mode in the README
cards.body: Scope: the section Theming of the README and the changelog entry. Steps: 1) explain how the theme is chosen (system preference, then the stored choice) and where the tokens live; 2) describe how to add a colour without breaking the dark theme; 3) follow the tone and the format of the existing texts of the project. Out of scope: changing the code, adding a feature, deciding the content plan. Acceptance criteria: nothing is stated that the sources do not say, the format of the project is respected and every text has its place. Proof: the files written and the list of the sources used.

cards.title: Final review of the fixes and of the documentation
cards.body: Scope: the fixes that came out of c5 and c6 and the text of c7. Steps: 1) check each finding of QA and design against the code that answers it; 2) run the build and the tests again and read the README against the real behaviour; 3) look for a regression next to the change, not only in it; 4) number each finding and say how to reproduce it. Out of scope: fixing what you find yourself. Acceptance criteria: every criterion of the card reviewed is checked one by one and the verdict follows from the findings. Proof: the numbered findings and the commands that were run.
